title: ExceptionalEvaluationSingleton
statement: Let O be a commutative ring, ell an element, T a scheme, and PE a StrictEtaleEvaluation as in def-per-strict-etale-system-interfaces. For every index n and derived finite-level object N with N in D>=a, there is a derived strict etale coefficient system M in D>=a whose n-th evaluation is isomorphic to N and whose other evaluations are zero. This uses the unrestricted system category, without cartesianness requirements.

source.place: Construction 4.1: exact coefficient evaluation; single-level section in the unrestricted system category.

proof.text: Put the module at index n, zero at every other index, and use zero transition maps. This defines a genuine additive functor. After any evaluation it is isomorphic to identity or zero. Evaluations jointly reflect isomorphisms and consequently jointly reflect finite limits and colimits. Thus the single-level functor is exact.

Take its canonical exact derived functor. The exact-localization universal property identifies evaluation with the derived identity or derived zero functor. Exactness preserves D>=a. These isomorphisms provide the asserted witness and vanishing.
